meta.source: 4 scoping calls (2026-04-14 to 2026-04-17) — Ashley Salerno, Brian Cook, Jean Jacobs, Venkat B

bizContext.snapshot: ‘So a lot of the times I will go through the backend and go through Home Depot reporting and find the deposits or not deposits the payment and then select the deposit paid box.’ — Ashley Salerno, April 2026 That step — and three others like it — are exactly what this engagement stops on go-live day. DataSkate is building four integrations to connect Home Depot Service Center, Salesforce, and ComputerEase into a single data path. HD Pro leads land in Salesforce within 10 minutes without a morning manual check (UC1). When a Salesforce quote is marked ‘Save as Final,’ a ComputerEase Job, Customer, and Budget Worksheet are created automatically — replacing the 1.5-hour-per-job rekey Ashley owns today (UC2). Signed contract PDFs are extracted and validated by MuleSoft IDP so document review becomes a resolved alert, not a morning task (UC3). When validation fails, a structured comment is written back to the HD screen automatically, replacing the hand-typed note (UC4). Most answers in this form are already filled in from your four scoping calls. Your job is to confirm they are correct and fill in the blanks — credentials and a few contacts we genuinely could not know. On go-live day, these stop: the manual morning HD lead check, the 1.5-hour-per-job ComputerEase rekey, the document-by-document contract review, and the hand-typed HD Portal exception comment.

journeyCards.label: Phase 1 — Connected
journeyCards.headline: HD Portal → Salesforce → ComputerEase becomes a single, instrumented data path
journeyCards.body: Things that stop on go-live Monday: the manual HD lead entry into Salesforce stops (UC1). The 1.5-hour-per-job ComputerEase rekey stops (UC2). The document-by-document contract review stops (UC3). The hand-typed HD Portal exception comment stops (UC4). The Quote Line Item is the canonical source for picket-type, material, and Wisconsin-specific deposit rules — no Excel sheets in the loop.

journeyCards.label: Phase 2 — Automated
journeyCards.headline: Triggers replace human dispatch on every step between lead and job entry
journeyCards.body: The deposit-paid status that Ashley manually looks up in HD Portal reporting every day syncs back into Salesforce automatically — closing her own aspiration: ‘if that could integrate and flow back through an API, that would work.’ ComputerEase job-status updates (in-progress, complete, paid) flow back into Salesforce so the team stops logging into Cameo to check milestones. Subcontract and commission worksheet write moves with the job header instead of becoming a second manual session.

journeyCards.label: Phase 3 — Agentic
journeyCards.headline: AgentForce reads the Salesforce data foundation Phase 1 built
journeyCards.body: Because Phase 1 created clean Salesforce objects keyed back to HD F-numbers and ComputerEase job numbers, an AgentForce agent answers the operational question Ashley spends her mornings on — without opening three systems.

internalFlags.bodyHtml:
INTERNAL TECHNICAL FLAGS — DO NOT SEND TO CLIENT

  1. CE Live Service is a P0 gate for UC2 and UC3: No ComputerEase API calls can be made until Deltek installs CE Live Service and provides the Deltek-managed integration URL. Development of UC2 cannot begin until this is unblocked. Estimated unblock: 1–2 weeks from Deltek ticket acknowledgement (4-hour legacy SLA per call).
  2. Sequential job-number write policy (FK-033): The integration MUST call CE’s next-id endpoint before each UC2 write. Never derive or self-allocate job numbers. UAT test writes must NOT consume the live job-number sequence — coordinate with Ashley on a test-safe approach (reserved test range or immediate delete after assertion).
  3. HD Portal write endpoints are unconfirmed (P1 blocker for UC4): UC4 exception write-back cannot be designed until HD Portal write endpoints are confirmed via Greg + Marius. Email fallback is designed as a degradation path. Treat UC4 as ‘design-in-parallel’ — email fallback is safe to build before HD endpoint confirmation.
  4. IDP two-stage pipeline (FK-034): Stage 1 (IDP extraction) and Stage 2 (DataWeave validation) must remain separate Mule flows. Never embed business-rule logic in the IDP extraction prompt. Unit tests for Stage 2 must pass without invoking IDP — use mock extraction JSON.
  5. CE production-only API (FK-032): All CE API testing (until Deltek provides a dev tenant) occurs in production with GET-only access group. Agree GET-only access group scope in writing with Peerless before first development run. Access group objects confirmed: Jobs, Subcontracts, Cost Types, Job Totals, Service Work Orders. Excluded: Payroll, Departments, Inventory, Vendors.
  6. GCP static IP ambiguity: Transcripts cite two IP addresses (35.222.218.224 and 135.226.22218). Brian Cook must confirm the canonical external IP before DataSkate adds it to any IP allowlist. Do not proceed with firewall configuration until resolved.
  7. SF External ID fields must exist before go-live: SF_HD_FNumber__c on Lead/Account/Quote and SF_CE_JobNumber__c on Quote must be created in Salesforce and marked as External ID before the integration goes live. If missing, all upserts will fall back to create-only and produce duplicates.
  8. Salesforce org flags open: Multi-currency, State/Country Picklists, and Shared Activities flags are unconfirmed from client. Each affects DWL transform logic for address and date fields. Confirm at kickoff before writing transforms.
  9. IDP scope=EMPTY requirement (FK-019): The Anypoint Connected App for IDP must have the OAuth scope field left EMPTY (not ‘urn:anypoint:idp’). Confirm with the Peerless Anypoint admin during kickoff — incorrect scope causes silent auth failures on first IDP submission.
  10. Single super-admin SPOF (Jean Jacobs) on ComputerEase: Jean’s PTO blocked all CE developer access for two days during scoping. Backup admin (Laura) must be provisioned and confirmed before development starts. This is a project-timeline risk, not just an ops risk.
